items.title: Omnigraph
items.summary: Open source graph database for your AI agents
items.body: Omnigraph is an open-source object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology. It allows AI agents safely collaborate on shared knowledge. Give agents one typed graph with Git-like branching, review, and merge for every write, so changes can be validated before becoming shared context. Run it on your own S3-compatible storage, with semantic, keyword, and hybrid search plus graph traversal in one query. No hosted memory API or proprietary storage required.

items.body:
Gemini Decisions API

Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question.

It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million.

Jev is text (and JSON) only. OpenAI can handle text and images.

items.body: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain.
